title: A beginning is a knot: a growth order never knots with the world
subject: What a growth order adds to a static law, read with the canonical knot test
conclusion: Written into a law, a growth history never knots with the world's states: on a fixed world the two form a product, and when worlds vary, with absent things forgotten, every knot containing an order variable contains an existence variable, which enters as a presence literal. The history's local part, which neighbour came first, is pairwise (2-CNF) and holds no knot, while time without a loop is a law whose knots are exactly the world's cycles, so on a ring the beginning is one not-all-equal knot over every seam, which the pairwise part contradicts. By Euler's count, sprouting grows only trees and disc moves only discs and spheres, and in one dimension the beginning does what no bounded static witness can: no radius-r law with bounded hidden labels tells a long thread from a ring.
